elements.quote: The effects of waiting time for outpatient psychotherapeutic interventions on patientreported outcomes in adolescents and adults with eating disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis
elements.reason: The title explicitly labels the work as a “systematic review and meta-analysis,” identifying it as a systematic review.

elements.quote: The effects of waiting time for outpatient psychotherapeutic interventions on patientreported outcomes in adolescents and adults with eating disorders
elements.reason: The title provides key objective information, specifying the exposure (waiting time for outpatient psychotherapeutic interventions), the outcome (patient-reported outcomes), and the population (adolescents and adults with eating disorders).

The retrieved evidence for the title does not report any supplementary information such as analysis method details beyond “meta-analysis,” included study designs, update status, or living-review status.

elements.reason: The abstract text describes an Objective and Methods but does not explicitly identify the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: Objective To assess the effects of waiting time for outpatient psychotherapeutic interventions on patient-reported outcomes in adolescents and adults with eating disorders.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an explicit statement of the main objective.

elements.quote: Quantitative studies of adolescents (≥ 10 years) and adults with eating disorders that examined waitlist conditions prior to outpatient psychotherapeutic interventions and measured eating disorder pathology with the Children's Eating Attitudes Test (chEAT) or Eating Disorder Examination-Questionnaire (EDE-Q) were eligible.
elements.reason: Main inclusion criteria are described, but explicit exclusion criteria are not reported in the provided abstract text.

elements.quote: Method MEDLINE, Embase, APA PsycInfo, CENTRAL and BASE were searched on 12 August 2025.
elements.reason: The abstract lists the information sources and includes the last search date.

elements.quote: Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 and ROBINS-I tools.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the risk-of-bias assessment methods/tools.

elements.quote: A within-group random-effects meta-analysis was performed assessing pre-post change scores of the EDE-Q Global Score (primary analysis) and EDE-Q subscales (secondary analyses).
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the methods used to present and synthesize results (within-group random-effects meta-analysis).

elements.quote: Results Nine waitlist-controlled studies (total n = 647, waitlisted n = 283) including adult participants with bulimia nervosa, binge-eating disorder and 'eating disorder not otherwise specified' met our eligibility criteria.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies and participants and summarizes relevant study/participant characteristics.

elements.quote: The pooled pre-post effect estimate was Hedges' g = - 0.17 (95% CI - 0.30 to - 0.05), indicating a negligible reduction in eating disorder pathology.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcome with the corresponding effect estimate and confidence interval.

elements.quote: The pooled pre-post effect estimate was Hedges' g = - 0.17 (95% CI - 0.30 to - 0.05)
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports the summary estimate and its 95% confidence interval.
The abstract reports within-group pre-post changes (waitlist-control pre-post), not comparisons between two groups where one group is favored.

elements.quote: Certainty of evidence was rated as moderate, given the high risk of bias across studies.
elements.reason: The abstract briefly summarizes an important limitation of the included evidence (high risk of bias) via the certainty rating.

elements.quote: Discussion Based on our results, waiting in waitlist control groups represents a period during which substantial eating disorder pathology and associated distress persist without therapeutic intervention.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an interpretation of the results and their implications.
No primary source of funding is reported in the provided abstract text.

elements.quote: A full protocol has been preregistered on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD420251090691).
elements.reason: The abstract provides the register name (PROSPERO) and registration number.

elements.quote: Participants entered the waiting period with high EDE-Q Global Scores, ranging from 3.08 to 4.65 across studies.
elements.reason: Provides some description of the current state of knowledge (high baseline eating disorder pathology during the waiting period), but does not explicitly describe important uncertainties or gaps in existing knowledge in the introduction/rationale.

elements.quote: Based on our results, waiting in waitlist control groups represents a period during which substantial eating disorder pathology and associated distress persist without therapeutic intervention. Further research is needed to better understand the effects of waiting time for regular eating disorder treatment outside a study setting.
elements.reason: Explains the importance/need in terms of the persistence of pathology and the call for further research, but does not clearly justify the review itself (e.g., why a new review is needed now) as part of existing knowledge.
No evidence found that, when similar systematic reviews exist, the need for the current review is explained with updates/replications and citations to previous systematic reviews.
No evidence found describing a proposed mechanism of action of the intervention (this review focuses on waiting time/control conditions rather than a described mechanistic rationale).
No evidence found that a logic model was used to show hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes.

elements.quote: The research question 'What are the effects of waiting time for outpatient psychotherapeutic interventions on PROs in adolescents and adults with AN, BN, BED and OSFED' was formulated using the Population, Exposure, Comparator, Outcome (PECO) framework (Additional file 1).
elements.reason: The review’s objective/research question is explicitly stated and formulated using the PECO framework.

Although PECO framework is mentioned, the planned comparisons for intervention effects (e.g., explicit comparator statement structured as PICO or appropriate variant) are not clearly stated in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Studies were included if they used an empirical, quantitative design, either randomised or non-randomised, such as RCTs, clinical trials, quasi-experimental studies or cohort studies; involved adolescents (≥ 10 years, according to the World Health Organization [72] definition) and/or adults (≥ 18 years) with AN, BN, BED or OSFED, according to DSM or International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems (ICD) (research) criteria that were valid at the time of diagnosis, or who exceeded validated cut-off values in questionnaires or interviews ... In addition ... Sub-BN and sub-BED had to be explicitly classified as OSFED for eligibility ... The ≥ 4 weeks cut-off for the waiting period of WLCGs was chosen ... included (a) compared an active psychotherapeutic intervention group (IG) in an outpatient setting with a WLCG or a no-treatment control group, or (b) retrospectively analysed a cohort ... In addition ... reported ED-specific PROs, measured using the Children's Eating Attitudes Test (chEAT) [73], Eating Disorder Examination-Questionnaire (EDEQ) [74] or EDE-Q 6.0 [75], for all study groups separately; and reported these PROs for a minimum of two time points: (1) ... (baseline), and (2) at least once at a subsequent time point ...
elements.reason: The text specifies eligibility-defining study characteristics, including study design, participant age and diagnostic criteria, intervention/comparator context (WLCGs vs no-treatment), outcome instruments, and follow-up/timepoint requirements.

elements.quote: Studies were included regardless of publication status. Both peer-reviewed and grey literature were considered. No restrictions were applied regarding publication year or language.
elements.reason: Eligibility criteria for report characteristics are explicitly stated for publication status, publication year, and language.
No evidence is provided describing how exclusion was distinguished between outcomes not measured versus outcome results not reported.
No evidence is provided specifying the groups used in each synthesis and how they link to comparisons defined in the review objectives.

elements.quote: The ≥ 4 weeks cut-off for the waiting period of WLCGs was chosen based on the EDE-Q reference period of 28 days.... Rationales for the exclusion criteria are provided in Additional file 3.
elements.reason: A rationale is provided for at least one notable restriction (the ≥4 weeks waiting-period cut-off), and it is stated that rationales for exclusion criteria are in Additional file 3, but the evidence does not show rationales for all notable restrictions.

elements.quote: The final search was executed on 12 August 2025 across all search engines.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the date when the information sources (search engines) were last searched.

elements.quote: MEDLINE (via Ovid; from 1946), Embase (via Ovid; from 1947), APA PsycInfo (via EBSCO; from 1887), CENTRAL and BASE were searched.
elements.reason: Names and platforms are provided for some bibliographic databases (MEDLINE, Embase, APA PsycInfo). However, available coverage dates are only explicitly given for MEDLINE/Embase/PsycInfo, while CENTRAL and BASE are listed without coverage dates.
No study registers, regulatory databases, or online repositories (beyond CENTRAL and BASE) are described with their names and any date restrictions.
The manuscript does not report any websites, search engines, or other online sources with their names and URLs in the provided evidence.
No organisations or manufacturers contacted to identify studies are named in the provided evidence.
No types of individuals contacted to identify studies are described in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: reference list checking of existing reviews and meta-analyses was performed manually
elements.reason: The types of reference lists examined are specified as reference lists of existing reviews and meta-analyses.

elements.quote: citation tracking, i.e. forward and backward citation searching, of the included studies was executed by MK using ResearchRabbit [97] on 9 October 2025.
elements.reason: The seed/citation tracking platform (ResearchRabbit) and the search date (9 October 2025) are explicitly reported for forward/backward citation searching.
The provided evidence does not describe any journals or conference proceedings consulted, including source names, dates covered, or search methods.

elements.quote: The final search strings for all engines can be found in Additional file 4.
elements.reason: The manuscript states that the complete final search strings are provided for all engines (databases/search engines) via Additional file 4.

elements.quote: No restrictions were applied regarding publication year or language.
elements.reason: Search limits are described (no restrictions on publication year/language), but the evidence does not explicitly justify these limits by reference to the eligibility criteria.

elements.quote: The search strategy was developed in Ovid MEDLINE by MK and piloted by searching seed papers [92-95]. It underwent peer review using the Peer Review of Electronic Search Strategies (PRESS) checklist [96], as well as review by an information specialist and a librarian.
elements.reason: The evidence describes development/piloting and peer review, but does not clearly report published search approaches/filters that were cited or any adaptations between sources.
No natural-language processing or text-analysis tools used to identify/refine search terms are mentioned in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence does not specify tools used to translate search strings between sources.

elements.quote: The search strategy was developed in Ovid MEDLINE by MK and piloted by searching seed papers [92-95].
elements.reason: A pilot of the search strategy is described (seed paper searching), but the evidence does not report broader validation studies/process beyond this piloting.

elements.quote: It underwent peer review using the Peer Review of Electronic Search Strategies (PRESS) checklist [96], as well as review by an information specialist and a librarian.
elements.reason: Peer review of the search strategy is described, including the use of the PRESS checklist and additional reviewers (information specialist and librarian).

elements.quote: Additional file 1. PECO framework.
elements.reason: The PECO framework is referenced, but the retrieved evidence does not describe the final conceptual structure/explorations used to develop the search structure.

elements.quote: Of the 8,269 records identified by the search engines, 2,527 were automatically marked as duplicates by TERA, which has been manually checked for and confirmed by MK (Fig. 1). During title/abstract screening, another 757 records were identified as duplicates by MK and PSM. A further 1,478 reports were identified by reference list checking and citation tracking. Of the 127 reports sought for retrieval, six were further duplicates and five could not be retrieved, resulting in 116 full texts assessed for eligibility.
elements.reason: Numbers of records/reports at screening-related stages (e.g., duplicates, full texts assessed for eligibility) are reported, but the number of reviewers screening each stage is not fully specified for each stage.

elements.quote: Screening was carried out independently by MK and either PSM or CT.
elements.reason: The review explicitly states that screening was performed independently and indicates which reviewers worked independently.

elements.quote: Any disagreements were resolved through discussion or, if consensus could not be reached, through consultation with AK.
elements.reason: A process for resolving screening disagreements (discussion, or consultation with AK if needed) is described.
Although the review reports contacting corresponding study authors for missing data values, it does not describe processes for obtaining/confirming eligibility information from investigators.

elements.quote: Reports written in languages other than English or German, i.e. Persian, Arabic and Dutch, were translated into English by native speakers.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes translation of non-English/German reports for eligibility assessment.

elements.quote: The Evidence Review Accelerator (TERA) [100] was used to manage study screening.
elements.reason: It is explicitly stated that TERA was used as an automation tool to manage the screening process.

elements.quote: Of the 8,269 records identified by the search engines, 2,527 were automatically marked as duplicates by TERA, which has been manually checked for and confirmed by MK (Fig. 1).
elements.reason: Externally derived automated classification is described (TERA automatically marked duplicates and manual checking/confirmation is described), but the requirement to identify externally derived classifiers by version or reference and to report how records removed are handled in the flow diagram is only partially met (TERA is referenced, but version is not specified and the flow-diagram reporting details are not shown in the provided evidence).
No internally derived classifiers (including training/validation details) are described in the retrieved evidence.
No machine-learning prioritisation tools or screening stopping/prioritisation rules are described in the retrieved evidence.
No crowdsourcing platforms and no integration of crowdsourcing into study selection are described in the retrieved evidence.
The evidence reports deduplication and duplicate detection, but it does not describe previously screened datasets specifically used to eliminate records, nor how such datasets were derived.

elements.quote: MK and PSM independently extracted data
elements.reason: It states that two reviewers (MK and PSM) extracted data, but it does not explicitly report how many reviewers collected data from each report in all cases.

elements.quote: MK and PSM independently extracted data, and MK and CT independently assessed risk of bias.
elements.reason: The text explicitly reports independent data extraction by multiple reviewers.

elements.quote: Again, any discrepancies were resolved through discussion or consultation with AK.
elements.reason: Processes for resolving disagreements/discrepancies between data collectors are described (discussion or consultation with AK).

elements.quote: Corresponding study authors were contacted if WLCG mean values or SDs of the EDE-Q Global Score or subscales for the two mandatory time points were missing.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes contacting study authors to obtain missing data.
No automation tools used for data collection (including their use, training, and validation) are described for the data extraction process.

elements.quote: Reports written in languages other than English or German, i.e. Persian, Arabic and Dutch, were translated into English by native speakers.
elements.reason: The methods used to translate non-English reports for the purpose of the review/data collection are specified.
The manuscript does not specify any software used to extract data from figures.

elements.quote: ED core behaviours assessed with the EDE-Q, reported as means with SDs, were only extracted if Global Scores and subscales were not reported and could not be obtained.
elements.reason: A conditional decision rule for extracting certain outcomes is described, but the criterion asks more broadly for decision rules when selecting data from multiple reports and resolving inconsistencies; those elements are not fully addressed in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: included a waiting period ≥ 4 weeks for the WLCG, no-treatment group or cohort of patients who ultimately received outpatient psychotherapy; reported ED-specific PROs, measured using the Children's Eating Attitudes Test (chEAT) [73], Eating Disorder Examination-Questionnaire (EDEQ) [74] or EDE-Q 6.0 [75], for all study groups separately; and reported these PROs for a minimum of two time points: (1) at or near the time of initial consultation, diagnostic workup, or study enrolment (baseline), and (2) at least once at a subsequent time point (i.e. at intervention start and/or at follow-up).
elements.reason: Outcome domains are partially listed (e.g., ED-specific PROs measured by chEAT/EDE-Q and the EDE-Q items including Global Score, subscales, and core behavior items), but a clear structured list of all outcome domains sought with explicit domain definitions is not fully provided in the retrieved text.

elements.quote: reported these PROs for a minimum of two time points: (1) at or near the time of initial consultation, diagnostic workup, or study enrolment (baseline), and (2) at least once at a subsequent time point (i.e. at intervention start and/or at follow-up).
elements.reason: The measurement time frame for outcome assessment is specified as baseline and at least one subsequent post-waiting time point (intervention start and/or follow-up).
The retrieved evidence does not state whether all compatible results within each outcome domain were sought (e.g., across all measures/time points/analyses) or how comprehensiveness was handled.

This conditional requirement depends on whether not all compatible results were sought; the retrieved evidence does not describe whether result selection was necessary or, if so, the selection process.

elements.quote: During the work process, the eligibility criteria have been amended once to ensure precision, clarity, and reproducibility. Additionally, the eligible patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) have been specified to enhance comparability between the individual studies. This specification was made in accordance with the ICHOM recommendations [33] to follow international consensus and ensure participation of persons with lived experience in the decision-making process.
elements.reason: The evidence reports amendments to eligibility criteria and specification of PROMs with stated rationales (precision/clarity/reproducibility; enhance comparability; align with ICHOM to follow consensus and include lived experience). However, it is not explicit that these amendments changed outcome-domain inclusion/definitions/importance specifically beyond the PROM specification.
The retrieved evidence does not describe changes to processes for selecting results within eligible outcome domains (including any rationales for such changes).

elements.quote: Generic PROs of well-being or functioning (measured using the KIDSCREEN-10 [85] or the WHO Disability Assessment Schedule 2.0 [86]), other mental healthrelated PROs, i.e. measures of anxiety, depression, and suicidal ideation..., as well as ED-specific QoL and social functioning (measured using the Clinical Impairment Assessment [91]) were eligible as secondary outcomes, but not required for inclusion.
elements.reason: The evidence indicates prioritisation between mandatory ED-specific PRO outcomes (required) and generic/other outcomes as secondary and not required. However, it does not clearly state which outcomes were considered most important *for interpreting the conclusions* or provide a rationale for prioritising the specific most-important outcomes.

elements.quote: A standardised data extraction form was developed and piloted on a small number of studies to ensure consistency across studies and between reviewers. Extracted data items are displayed in Additional file 5.
elements.reason: The review states that extracted data items are presented (Additional file 5), but the evidence provided here does not list and define all the “other variables” that were sought; it only indicates the existence/location of the item list and describes some specific variables (e.g., funding sources, conflicts of interest, EDE-Q means/SDs) without fully enumerating and defining them.

elements.quote: For Arcelus et al. [104], post-waiting means and post-waiting SDs were unavailable and could not be obtained by contacting the corresponding author. Post-waiting means were derived by adding the reported mean difference (MD) to the pre-waiting mean. As proposed by Morris [105] and Morris and DeShon [106], SDs in pre- and post-test populations can be assumed equal. However, to increase the precision we approximated post-waiting SDs by multiplying the pre-waiting SD by the average proportional change in SDs from pre to post observed in the remaining included studies.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes assumptions and derivation methods used when post-waiting information was missing/unavailable (deriving means from MD, assuming pre/post SD equality, and approximating SDs via proportional change).

The evidence provided does not cite any tool used to determine which data items to collect. While it mentions that a standardised data extraction form was developed and piloted, it does not explicitly describe citing a tool for deciding which data items were collected.

elements.quote: For risk of bias assessment at the results level, the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool [107] was used for RCTs, and the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomised Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool [108] for NRSIs.
elements.reason: The tools used (RoB 2 and ROBINS-I) are specified, but no tool versions are reported.

elements.quote: Domains: D1: Bias arising from the randomization process. D2: Bias due to deviations from the intended intervention. D3: Bias due to missing outcome data. D4: Bias in measurement of the outcome. D5: Bias in selection of the reported result.
elements.reason: The domains/components assessed for RoB 2 are explicitly listed.

elements.quote: Overall judgement for each study followed the respective algorithms.
elements.reason: It is reported that an overall risk-of-bias judgement was made and that the study-level judgement followed the algorithms.

elements.quote: Given the reversed logic of our objective, we adapted these tools by considering the control condition, i.e. the waitlist, as the intervention.
elements.reason: The adaptation to both RoB 2 and ROBINS-I is described (treating the waitlist as the intervention).
No newly developed risk-of-bias tool is reported in the available evidence.

elements.quote: MK and PSM independently extracted data, and MK and CT independently assessed risk of bias. Again, any discrepancies were resolved through discussion or consultation with AK.
elements.reason: The number of reviewers for risk-of-bias assessment (MK and CT), their independence, and the disagreement resolution approach (discussion/consultation with AK) are reported.

The evidence describes contacting corresponding authors for missing study outcome statistics (e.g., WLCG mean values or SDs), but it does not describe processes to obtain or confirm risk-of-bias information from study investigators.

elements.quote: Traffic light plot generated using robvis [142]
elements.reason: An automation tool (robvis) is mentioned for visualisation, but the evidence does not report details on training, performance, or validation of automation for the risk-of-bias assessment process.

elements.quote: The pooled effect estimate was Hedges' g = - 0.17 (95% CI - 0.30 to - 0.05), indicating a small symptom reduction (Fig. 4).
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies the effect measure used for synthesized results (Hedges' g) and reports pooled effect estimates for multiple outcomes (e.g., Global Score and subscales such as Restraint, Weight Concern, Shape Concern, Eating Concern).
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect sizes (and their rationale) are reported in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence does not describe any re-expression of synthesized results using another effect measure.

elements.quote: Effects of waiting time were analysed using Hedges' g to correct for small sample sizes [119], with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) calculated using the Wald method [120].
elements.reason: A rationale is provided for choosing Hedges' g (correction for small sample sizes), but the retrieved evidence does not fully justify the choice of effect measure(s) across all contexts/outcomes beyond this statement.

elements.quote: During the work process, the eligibility criteria have been amended once to ensure precision, clarity, and reproducibility. Additionally, the eligible patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) have been specified to enhance comparability between the individual studies. This specification was made in accordance with the ICHOM recommendations [33] to follow international consensus and ensure participation of persons with lived experience in the decision-making process. The amendments were made prior to data extraction and have been documented in version 2.0 of the registration record. Rationales for the exclusion criteria are provided in Additional file 3.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes how eligibility criteria (and eligible PROMs) were defined and amended prior to data extraction, including where rationales are provided. However, it does not explicitly describe the processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each synthesis (e.g., how studies were tabulated/compared against planned synthesis groups).

elements.quote: Corresponding study authors were contacted if WLCG mean values or SDs of the EDE-Q Global Score or subscales for the two mandatory time points were missing. For Schlup et al. [101], we received EDE-Q unguided self-help or other interventions that do not include contact with a mental health professional or mental health trainee (postgraduate), pharmacotherapeutic treatment without an active psychotherapeutic intervention, or. other forms of therapy that are not psychotherapeutic in approach, such as movement, art or nutrition therapy. Global Score and subscale means with SDs for both time points from the authors. Data for Krohmer et al. [102] was extracted from the supplemental material [103]. For Arcelus et al. [104], post-waiting means and post-waiting SDs were unavailable and could not be obtained by contacting the corresponding author. Post-waiting means were derived by adding the reported mean difference (MD) to the pre-waiting mean. As proposed by Morris [105] and Morris and DeShon [106], SDs in pre- and post-test populations can be assumed equal. However, to increase the precision we approximated post-waiting SDs by multiplying the pre-waiting SD by the average proportional change in SDs from pre to post observed in the remaining included studies.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes data-preparation methods for synthesis, including how missing statistics were handled (contacting authors when WLCG means/SDs were missing) and how missing/insufficient summary statistics were converted/derived (deriving post-waiting means from MD, assuming/approximating post-waiting SDs).

elements.quote: Results were displayed in outcome tables, synthesised narratively and summarised in a 'Summary of Findings' table.
elements.reason: The manuscript states that results were presented in outcome tables and a 'Summary of Findings' table, but the specific tabular structures and the exact data included in them are not described in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Visual inspection of the funnel plot for the primary analysis of the Global Score (Fig. 9) and the secondary analyses of the subscales did not suggest pronounced asymmetry. Fig. 8 Forest plot for the secondary analysis of the EDE-Q subscale Eating Concern Fig. 9 Funnel plot for the primary analysis of the EDE-Q Global Score
elements.reason: The retrieved evidence explicitly describes graphical methods used to display results (forest plot and funnel plot), including where they appear (Figs. 8 and 9).
No retrieved evidence reports the basis for ordering or grouping studies within tables or graphs.
No retrieved evidence reports any rationale for using non-standard graphs.

elements.quote: All statistical analyses were performed in R (version 4.5.2) [98] using the metafor package (version 4.8.0) [110].
elements.reason: Reports the statistical software (R) and package (metafor) with version numbers used for the meta-analysis.
